headline: FILM STRIPS shipped — visual PRs now show their own before/after
lede: A seeded replay runs on main and on the branch, the same checkpoints are photographed through the game contract, and one verdict line says whether the PR is visual-only or changed the simulation. #1216.

notes.text: npm run filmstrip -- --game tetris --attach <pr> publishes a two-row strip (base vs head, ticks 150/300/450/600) to the telemetry CDN and comments it inline on the PR; /retrogames/forge/report gained a film-strips section (shiftreportcheck 126/126).

A hex hash where a decimal was expected was the clue: a double-slash URL (/retrogames//game) silently mounted the WRONG game. Capture now proves meta.id, dev-server probes hit the slashed base (vite 404s the bare path) and bind localhost (IPv6-only), never 127.0.0.1.

The verdict splits honestly: state-hash equality proves sim alignment, pixel diffs show what the eye should see; a built-in seed+1 mutant in filmstripcheck (16/16) proves the tool can still call divergence.
